assessment: Confirmed the candidate/default-open flow and dashboard mismatch. ControlCenterRules.BuildExceptions recomputes current exceptions as records with no status. ControlCenterQueryService.GetExceptionsAsync overlays a persisted state when present and otherwise returns lowercase open. SetExceptionStatusHandler accepts and persists only lowercase acknowledged/resolved, and the repository has no other ControlExceptionStates writer or open-row seeder. The integration test creates a large-refund candidate, observes default open, then acknowledges and reads it back. OwnerDashboardQueryService instead counts only persisted rows where Status equals capitalized Open; it neither builds candidates nor defaults missing states. Thus a newly generated open candidate is absent from dashboard count; after action the persisted row is acknowledged/resolved. Case-insensitive SQL comparison cannot supply a missing candidate row. This strongly confirms a stale/ordinarily-zero dashboard projection. Counterevidence: the dedicated Control Center continues to surface and review dynamic exceptions; exact owner reliance and legacy manually inserted uppercase Open rows are unverified. Severity should remain candidate pending root disposition; runtime not executed.
